questions.question: Looking far ahead while driving is:

options.text: Not helpful, since you cannot do anything about hazards far away.
Good practice to spot hazards early.
Only required when carrying hazardous materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: Good practice to spot hazards early.
questions.explanation: Good drivers look 12 to 15 seconds ahead. This gives you time to see hazards early and respond safely.

questions.question: In heavy fog, you should:
questions.explanation: Driving in fog is very dangerous. If you can, do not drive in foggy conditions.

questions.question: What is another name for the service line?
questions.explanation: The service line is also called the control line or signal line. It sends air to the trailer brakes and is controlled by the foot brake or hand brake.

questions.question: Unbaffled tanks are also called ____ tanks.
questions.explanation: Unbaffled tanks are also called smooth bore tanks.

questions.question: Don't look at one mirror for too long because:

options.text: Looking at mirrors can make you tired.
You may drive a long distance without looking at the road.
The mirror may not show an accurate view.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may drive a long distance without looking at the road.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often but quickly. Staring at one mirror too long can cause you to drive far without seeing what is ahead.

questions.question: Hydraulic brakes can fail because of:
questions.explanation: Hydraulic brakes often fail when pressure is lost. They can also fade from too much use on long downhill grades.

questions.question: Which material may need a transport index?
questions.explanation: Some radioactive materials need a transport index. This number shows how much control the material needs during transport. The total transport index for all cargo in one vehicle cannot exceed 50.

questions.question: ____ is a thin layer of ice on road surfaces.
questions.explanation: Black ice is a thin, clear layer of ice. You can see the road through it, so it looks like wet pavement.

questions.question: Which is not a rule for using turn signals?

options.text: Signal the whole time you are turning.
Turn off your signal after your turn or lane change is complete.
Only signal if another vehicle is near.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only signal if another vehicle is near.
questions.explanation: Always signal before turning or changing lanes, even if no other vehicles are near. Start signaling well ahead and keep it on during the entire turn. Turn it off when the turn is complete.

questions.question: If there are two left turn lanes, which one should you use?

options.text: Large vehicles should not turn where there are two left turn lanes.

questions.explanation: Large vehicles need extra space to make left turns. Use the right turn lane to start your turn when two left lanes are available.

questions.question: A driver should make sure that:

options.text: The shipping paper matches the markings and labels on the packages.
The shipping paper is written in code.
All packages are labeled as poison.
The shipping paper is not in the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: The shipping paper matches the markings and labels on the packages.
questions.explanation: Check that the shipping paper matches the package markings and labels. Make sure the shipper included the correct description on the shipping paper and that it matches what is on the packages.

questions.question: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS):

options.text: Makes a loud squeaking noise when used.
Helps you stay in control while braking.

questions.correctAnswerText: Helps you stay in control while braking.
questions.explanation: ABS gives you better control when braking. It does not change how far your vehicle travels before it stops.

questions.question: Shipping papers for hazardous materials should be:

options.text: At the bottom of a stack of shipping papers.
On top of a stack of shipping papers.

questions.correctAnswerText: On top of a stack of shipping papers.
questions.explanation: Drivers and carriers need to find hazardous materials papers quickly. These papers should always be on top of the stack.

questions.question: When you leave your vehicle, you should:
questions.explanation: Always set the parking brake when you leave your vehicle.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Make eye contact with the other driver.
Assume the other driver doesn't see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Assume the other driver doesn't see you.
questions.explanation: Always assume that other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians cannot see you. Be ready for them to suddenly move into your path. You can lightly tap your horn or flash your lights as you pass.

questions.question: When stopped on the side of the road, a driver should:

options.text: Keep the driver's side door open.

questions.explanation: If you must stop on the side of the road, turn on your emergency flashers to warn other drivers. This is especially important at night.

questions.question: What does a tractor protection valve do?

options.text: Keeps air in the brake system if there is a major leak.
Prevents the truck from being stolen.
Prevents the driver from going too fast.
Prevents the trailer from accidentally disconnecting.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keeps air in the brake system if there is a major leak.
questions.explanation: In a combination vehicle with air brakes, the tractor protection valve protects the truck's brake system if the trailer breaks away or leaks air.

questions.question: Air pressure in the ____ air line is controlled by the foot brake or trailer hand brake.
questions.explanation: The service air line (also called the control or signal line) is controlled by the foot brake or trailer hand brake. This line connects to relay valves that make the trailer brakes work faster.

questions.question: Texting while driving a commercial motor vehicle is:

options.text: Acceptable if the text is work-related.
Acceptable if the text has fewer than 10 words.
Encouraged because it is safer than talking on the phone.

questions.explanation: Texting while driving a commercial motor vehicle is illegal and dangerous. This includes typing text or reading text from any electronic device.

questions.question: In an emergency situation, you should:

options.text: Always turn on flashers to warn other drivers.

questions.explanation: Stopping is not always the safest choice in an emergency. It is usually safer to steer out of the way to avoid a crash.
